items.q: What happens in your brain when you're put on the spot?
items.a: Your brain hits the **panic button** and opens **a dozen browser tabs**. Without a fallback structure, you verbalize messy thoughts and lose **clarity, authority, and confidence**.

items.q: What do frameworks replace when pressure hits?
items.a: When you have a framework, you **fall back on the framework instead** of panic-scrambling. Less than **10%** of Vinh's workshop audience already used communication frameworks.
**3 steps**, **2 types** (or two ways), or **the 1 thing**. It is a **listicle scaffold**, not a script — structure for impromptu answers under pressure.

items.q: Do you need to deliver all three modes in one answer?
items.a: No. **Pick one mode only** — whichever fits fastest. One structured path is enough to sound clear; you don't stack all three variants.

items.q: How does 3-2-1 work on a random topic like avocados?
items.a: **One thing**: great for keto. **Two ways**: toast vs fruit. **Three steps**: cut, mash, season. Same menu works for "travel": one word, two types, or plan → book → go.

items.q: How do you train 3-2-1 for real Q&A?
items.a: Use a **random topic + 3-second countdown**. In the demo, the student answered before the countdown finished because the framework made her **feel ready**.

items.q: How does having a framework change your body language?
items.a: Without one you're **scared and shrink** from the mic. With one you **lean in and walk toward the audience** — readiness shows up physically before the words do.
